```{r}
df <- read_csv("../../01_data/4_model/raw_model_dataset.csv", col_types = cols(datetime = col_skip()))
df
```

```{r}
summary(df)
```

```{r}
# mark categorical variables
df$year <- factor(df$year)
# set 2025 as base year
df$year <- relevel(df$year, ref = "2025")

df$season <- factor(df$season)
df$time_of_day <- factor(df$time_of_day)
df$peak_hour <- factor(df$peak_hour)
df$heating_dd <- factor(df$heating_dd)
df$cap_threshold <- factor(df$cap_threshold)
```

```{r}
# check correlation among numerical variables

cor_matrix <- cor(df %>% select(where(is.numeric)), use = "complete.obs")
print(cor_matrix)

corrplot(cor_matrix, method ="circle", addCoef.col=TRUE)

```

```{r}
cor_by_year <- df %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  group_split() %>%
  setNames(unique(df$year)) %>%
  lapply(function(x) {
    x %>% select(where(is.numeric)) %>% cor(method = "pearson")
  })
cor_by_year
```
```{r}
# cut out values for log(rtm_price) < 0
df_sub <- df[df$rtm_price > 2.3, ]
```

```{r, include=False}
# stepwise regression

# Fit the full model 
Full <- lm(log10(rtm_price) ~ spare_capacity + ng_price_monthly + season + 
    time_of_day + cap_threshold + year + degree_days + peak_hour + heating_dd, data = df_sub)   
# Find the MSE for the full model 
MSE <- (summary(Full)$sigma)^2 
# Start with a model with NO predictors 
none <- lm(log10(rtm_price) ~ 1, data = df_sub) 
# DON’T specify a direction 
step(none, scope = list(upper=Full), scale=MSE)
```

```{r}
mod_selected <- lm(log10(rtm_price) ~ spare_capacity + ng_price_monthly + 
    season + cap_threshold + time_of_day + heating_dd + degree_days + 
    year + peak_hour, data = df_sub)
summary(mod_selected)
plot(mod_selected)
```

```{r}
# cross validation steps
library(caret)
library(randomForest)

# set threshold for capacity
df_sub$cap_threshold <- df_sub$spare_capacity > 0.9

# 1. Split into train/test
set.seed(42)
train_idx <- createDataPartition(df_sub$rtm_price, p = 0.8, list = FALSE)
train_data <- df_sub[train_idx, ]
test_data  <- df_sub[-train_idx, ]

# 2. Define cross-validation scheme (5-fold CV)
ctrl <- trainControl(
  method = "cv",
  number = 5,
  savePredictions = "final"
)

# 3. Train model with CV
set.seed(42)
model <- train(
  log10(rtm_price) ~ spare_capacity + ng_price_monthly + 
    season + cap_threshold + time_of_day + heating_dd + degree_days + 
    year + peak_hour,
  data = train_data,
  method = "lm",
  trControl = ctrl
)

print(model$results)

# 4. Evaluate on held-out test set
pred_test <- predict(model, newdata = test_data)
postResample(pred_test, log10(test_data$rtm_price))   # RMSE, Rsquared, MAE
```

```{r}
# plot train and test predictions
train_preds <- predict(model, newdata = train_data)
test_preds  <- predict(model, newdata = test_data)

plot_df <- bind_rows(
  data.frame(actual = log10(train_data$rtm_price), predicted = train_preds, set = "Train", spare_capacity = train_data$spare_capacity),
  data.frame(actual = log10(test_data$rtm_price), predicted = test_preds, set = "Test", spare_capacity = test_data$spare_capacity)
)

ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = actual, y = predicted, color = set)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.5, alpha = 0.8) +
  coord_fixed(xlim = c(0.3, 3.8), ylim = c(0.3, 3.8)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray40") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Train" = "#1f77b4", "Test" = "#d62728")) +
  labs(title = "Predicted vs. Actual log10(rtm Price)", x = "Actual", y = "Predicted", color = "Data Set")
# actual
ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = spare_capacity, y = actual, color = set)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.5, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Train" = "#1f77b4", "Test" = "#d62728")) +
  labs(title = "Actual log10(rtm Price) vs. spare capacity metric", x = "spare capacity metric", y = "actual price (log10)", color = "Data Set")
# predicted
ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = spare_capacity, y = predicted, color = set)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.5, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Train" = "#1f77b4", "Test" = "#d62728")) +
  labs(title = "Predicted log10(rtm Price) vs. spare capacity metric", x = "spare capacity metric", y = "predicted price (log10)", color = "Data Set")
```
